q: A RAG app indexes HR policies that are reloaded into a Delta table once a night. The team wants the cheapest setup that keeps the index current by the next morning. What should they configure?
o: A Direct Vector Access index updated by the application
A Delta Sync index with CONTINUOUS sync
A Delta Sync index with TRIGGERED sync, and a `sync()` call after the nightly load
A storage-optimized endpoint with CONTINUOUS sync
e: The data changes once a day and already lives in Delta, so a TRIGGERED Delta Sync index refreshed after the load is enough. CONTINUOUS sync runs all the time and costs more, and storage-optimized endpoints do not support it.

q: You add MLflow scorers to monitor a live support agent. Production traffic has no expected answers. Which scorer can you NOT use there?
o: `Correctness`
`RetrievalGroundedness`
`Safety`
`RelevanceToQuery`
e: `Correctness` compares the response with expected facts, so it needs ground truth. The other three judge the request, context and response only, which is why they can run on live traces.

q: A source folder holds scanned contracts saved as PDF images. Text extraction with `pypdf` returns almost nothing. What is the right fix?
o: Use `beautifulsoup4` to parse the PDFs
Run OCR, for example with `pytesseract`, or a layout-aware parser such as `ai_parse_document()`
Increase the chunk overlap
Switch to an embedding model with a longer context
e: Scanned pages contain images of text, not text. They need OCR or a document parser that handles images. HTML parsers and chunking settings do not help when no text was extracted.

q: Users ask an assistant "When will order 48213 arrive?". The vector index holds shipping policies only, and answers are vague. What change fixes this?
o: Give the agent a tool that looks up the order by its ID in a structured table
Fine-tune the LLM on last month's orders
Add a re-ranker on top of the policy index
Increase `num_results` from 5 to 50
e: Per-order facts are keyed data that change daily. A structured lookup (a UC function or Genie over the orders table) returns the exact value. Fine-tuning goes stale and retrieval settings cannot find facts that are not in the index.

q: Evaluation shows the correct policy chunk is often not among the top 50 candidates returned by Vector Search. The team plans to add a cross-encoder re-ranker. What should you tell them?
o: Good idea: re-ranking raises recall in the first stage
Re-ranking only works with Direct Vector Access indexes
Re-ranking only reorders the candidates it gets, so first fix recall: chunking, hybrid search or filters
Re-ranking removes the need for an evaluation set
e: A re-ranker improves the precision and order of the final context, but it cannot recover documents the first stage missed. Low recall is fixed in retrieval itself: better chunks, hybrid search, query rewriting or a larger k.
